sections.content:
160,720 people

were counted on the census as "generalist medical practitioners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Generalist medical practitioners diagnose mental and physical injuries, disorders and diseases, prescribe and give treatment, recommend preventative action, and conduct medical education and research activities.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "generalist medical practitioners", 20.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "generalist medical practitioners" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "generalist medical practitioners" included:

  • veterinarians
  • speech and language therapists
  • solicitors and lawyers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "generalist medical practitioners" there were a similar number of men and women (46.1% compared with 53.9%).

This means "generalist medical practitioners" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 46.1% and women made up 53.9% of "generalist medical practitioners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "generalist medical practitioners" included:

  • telephone salespersons
  • leisure and theme park attendants
  • buyers and procurement officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "generalist medical practitioners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "generalist medical practitioners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "generalist medical practitioners", 5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (81.2% compared with 18.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (79.5%) than self-employed (20.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
